holidays.name: National Pumpkin Pie Day
holidays.description: A day devoted to the spiced orange custard slice that somehow gets a second round of glory after Thanksgiving. Leftover pie for breakfast is not just allowed, it is practically the official ritual.
holidays.origin: Part of the loose American calendar of unofficial food days, which tends to attach dessert celebrations to dates when the food is already on the table. Pumpkin pie traces back to early colonial cooks who baked spiced pumpkin in crusts.
holidays.funFact: Early colonists made a version of pumpkin pie by hollowing out a pumpkin, filling it with milk, spices, and honey, then baking it whole in hot ashes.

holidays.name: Newton's Birthday (Isaac Newton Day)
holidays.description: Nerds and physics fans celebrate the birth of Sir Isaac Newton, who gave us gravity, the laws of motion, and calculus. Some celebrate by dropping apples, which is gloriously on theme.
holidays.origin: Under the Julian calendar used in England at the time, Newton was born on December 25, 1642. Under the Gregorian calendar his birthday falls on January 4, 1643. Fans of the Julian date jokingly claim he shares a birthday with Christmas, and the humorous term Newtonmas was born.
holidays.funFact: Newtonmas is a tongue-in-cheek holiday for science lovers, and some people celebrate by giving gifts of books on physics or by decorating trees with apples instead of ornaments.

holidays.name: National Date Nut Bread Day
holidays.description: A salute to the humble, dense, sweet loaf studded with dates and walnuts, a dessert-bread hybrid that your grandmother probably served with cream cheese. It is a perfect holiday-season snack that rarely gets the spotlight it deserves.
holidays.origin: This is one of the unofficial American food days that cluster around the end of December. Date nut bread became popular in the early 20th century when canned and packaged dates became widely available in home kitchens, and it was often a staple at holiday tea tables.
holidays.funFact: In the 1920s and 30s, date nut bread with cream cheese sandwiches were a popular tea-room lunch item, and the combination was considered quite fancy and a bit exotic.

holidays.name: Atheist Solidarity / Festivus Eve Observance
holidays.description: The day after Festivus Eve is the prime time for those who grew up with the Seinfeld holiday invented as an alternative to the commercial December rush. It is the standard hangover day from the Airing of Grievances and Feats of Strength, both parts of the spoof tradition.
holidays.origin: Festivus is celebrated on December 23 and was created by writer Dan O'Keefe's father, then popularized by the 1997 Seinfeld episode The Strike. The days following are often used by fans to recap their grievances and wrestling matches.
holidays.funFact: The Festivus pole is made of unadorned aluminum because, according to Frank Costanza, it has a very high strength-to-weight ratio, and it requires no decoration.

holidays.name: Quiet Christmas Day Observance: Christmas Pickle Day
holidays.description: Families hide a glass pickle ornament deep in the Christmas tree branches, and the first child to find it supposedly gets an extra gift or a year of good luck. It is one of the most delightfully odd tree traditions.
holidays.origin: Often claimed to be a German tradition, though most Germans have never heard of it. The story may have been boosted by marketing in the late 19th century by ornament sellers, and some tell of a Civil War soldier from Bavaria whose pickle plea saved his life.
holidays.funFact: A 2016 survey found that a large majority of Germans had never heard of the Christmas pickle, and many said they thought it was an American tradition.
